If you restrict yourself to Java you will have a hard time as it is widely considered not to be a good language for game programming. Combine that with the fact that developing an engine is really, really difficult and thus the landscape of open source engines across all languages is scattered with half-finnished projects and those that can be used are either tailored to very specific use cases (eg only 2D or only for FPS) or not actual game engines but frame works or very simplistic... or have major drawbacks. To put things into perspective: The cost of developing an engine as used by AAA games starts at tens of millions and goes well beyond the 100 million mark. Now, as a single person you won't be able to utilize those large engines so you are probably looking for something small that does a few specific things well.

So, rather than listing all the engines, engine frameworks or libs I know and have worked with, I'll answer with a question: What kind of game are you planning to create? Do you even want an engine, or maybe an engine frame work or just a graphics API?

Second this. I would go with the C# and MonoGames (XNA) developed on Xamarin or Visual Studio. If you're comfortable with Java learning C# shouldn't take that long and MonoGames is basic enough to get you started.

LibGDX is pretty good if you're willing to put the time in to make what you want out of it.

Personally I'd recommending using C# instead, with either Monogame or Unity. I personally prefer Monogame for 2D projects and Unity for 3D.

I would check out JMonkey. I played around with it a bit and it seemed pretty cool. Like most people say Java isn't the best language for game development, But Notch Persson is a billionaire now. That being said, It's a good place to start if you want to learn how game development works without picking up a new language at the same time.
